recognize_zh: 周邊血中多顆嗜中性白血球胞質內吞入完整紅血球（紅血球吞噬，erythrophagocytosis），核被推擠成新月形，並伴隨空泡與毒性顆粒；D 圖見紅血球凝集，背景有棘狀紅血球，提示 Donath-Landsteiner 抗體所致的陣發性冷血紅素尿症（PCH）。
features: Neutrophils containing one or more intact ingested red cells within phagocytic vacuoles (panels A-C, E)
Neutrophil nuclei compressed and displaced into crescentic or C-shaped contours around the engulfed red cells
Cytoplasmic vacuolation and coarse toxic granulation in phagocytic neutrophils
Small cluster of agglutinated red cells (panel D)
Background red cells with crenated/echinocytic forms and occasional spherocyte-like dense cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous neutrophils with erythrophagocytosis, containing one or more intact red cells within cytoplasmic vacuoles that displace and compress the nucleus into a crescent, accompanied by additional vacuoles and toxic granulation. A small red cell agglutinate is present, and background red cells include crenated forms and occasional dense spherocyte-like cells. No organisms are identified. In a patient with acute hemolysis, florid neutrophil erythrophagocytosis is suggestive of paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria; a direct antiglobulin test (C3 positive) and Donath-Landsteiner test are recommended.

ddx.vs: Warm AIHA shows prominent spherocytes with IgG-positive DAT and erythrophagocytosis by neutrophils is rare, whereas PCH is C3-only DAT-positive with a biphasic Donath-Landsteiner antibody.
Cold agglutinin disease shows large red cell agglutinates on the smear with a high-titer IgM cold agglutinin, and neutrophil erythrophagocytosis is not a typical feature.
HLH erythrophagocytosis is performed by macrophages in marrow or tissue, not by circulating neutrophils, and is accompanied by cytopenias, hyperferritinemia and fever.

ddx.dx: In vitro artifact from delayed processing/EDTA storage
ddx.vs: Storage-related phagocytosis is sparse, and the florid, widespread engulfment with hemolytic clinical findings favors an in vivo process.

captions: A: neutrophil with an engulfed red cell and crescentic compressed nucleus
B: two neutrophils, one containing an ingested red cell with vacuoles
C: neutrophils with phagocytosed red cells and vacuoles
